pairs.why: A's umbrella has soft, smooth scalloped panels with no visible ribs, like the real card; B's exposed spokes and harder shine make it read as a different, more mechanical object.
B's fewer, broader, softly rounded panels match the real umbrella's colour blocks better than A's many narrow scalloped segments, though the two are close.
A fills the frame with a tall glass and big chunky ice cubes, and the straw sits inside the drink, all close to the real card; B is a small, distant glass with tiny ice.
A's large glass, clear crisp highlights, and straw running through the juice match the real card's framing and build; B is undersized in the frame.
A's flared, swollen glass and heavy glow push it toward toy-like gloss, while B's neater, straight-sided glass is built more like the real one, even though it is too small.
B is glossy, neon, and plastic, which is too toy-like; A's matte salmon-pink coral and muted rocks are closer to the real card, even though A is somewhat busier.
The two are nearly identical; B's slightly darker, more muted green and calmer brightness sit a little closer to the real card.
A's main coral is pinker and its colours sit closer to the real card's salmon-pink, while B leans red; rendering and texture are otherwise about equal.
